answers.answer: Shuffle the nine region cards; reveal one for the King’s region. Each player draws another region card for their home region and places their Grande there. Each starts with ten Caballeros: two in the home region, one on the first success-track space, and seven in court.

In round 1, players choose the starter. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the previous round leads; others play clockwise. No power-card value already played that round may be matched.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “No value already played this round may be matched.”

answers.answer: Turns proceed in descending power-card value. At the start of a turn, recruit up to the allowance shown on the power card from provinces into court; then choose an available action card.
If your provinces lack enough, take your own Caballeros from the board to make up the difference. The King’s region is taboo and Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.

Ordinary deployment moves up to the action card’s number from your court to regions adjacent to the King’s current region and/or the Castillo. You may divide the allowance among destinations, deploy fewer or none, and the activity cannot be split/interleaved with the special action.
They may be done in either order, but each activity must be completed before starting the other; neither may be split or interleaved. The special action may be declined.

Set the selected card aside after your turn so later players cannot choose it; after all turns, discard unselected face-up cards. The King card is revealed again each round and is never permanently discarded.
No Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of the King’s region. It may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected.
Clearly announce how many Caballeros enter the Castillo. King location does not restrict entry. Caballeros leave only during general scoring; no action removes them earlier.

After rounds 3, 6, and 9: (1) secretly choose one destination per player before uncovering Castillo, excluding the King’s region; all of a player’s Castillo pieces go to one destination; (2) uncover and score Castillo; (3) reveal disks and move pieces to destinations, except pieces assigned to the King’s region go to their owners’ courts, then replace the empty Castillo; (4) score the nine regions in scoring-track order.
answers.evidence: General scoring after rounds 3, 6 and 9, stages 1–4.

answers.answer: Each player must send all their Castillo Caballeros to one region, so they cannot split them or keep them in Castillo. The destination is selected secretly before Castillo is uncovered; the King’s region is not a legal disk choice. If a player’s pieces are assigned there, they go to that player’s court.
The three players tied at four each score 3 each; the player with three scores 1. Grandes do not count toward majority.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: five-player example and Grande rule.

answers.answer: The players with 4, 3, and 2 each score 6, 4, and 0 respectively; the other player with 2 also scores 0.
In two-player games only first place can pay; in three-player games first and second can pay. A two-player tie for first shifts to second place, which is outside the payable ranks, so neither scores.

When the relevant region is scored, including special scoring, the sole majority holder in the King’s region gets +2; the sole majority holder with their own Grande in a region gets +2 home bonus. Neither bonus applies on a tie for first.
Special scoring reveals and scores Castillo, then covers the same Caballeros again. It neither empties nor redistributes them.
answers.evidence: Actions: protected locations; Stack 3 Castillo row.

answers.answer: A mobile scoreboard may be placed at Castillo; it cannot move into or out of the King’s region. The two scoreboards cannot be stacked, and they must stay right-side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0, without rotation. It can be moved to another region.

Move your Grande to another region except the King’s region or Castillo; it cannot leave the King’s region. The destination may already contain several Grandes. The destination becomes your new home region.
The recovery action returns any one of your played power cards, including the one played this turn. You need not reveal which, though taking the visible top card is apparent.
The game ends after all stages of the third general scoring after round 9. The player furthest along the success track wins; no additional endgame tiebreaker is given.

Separate action cards by the 1–5 Caballeros on their backs, shuffle each stack separately, and place face down. At the start of each round reveal the top card of all five stacks. Standard round marker starts at 1.
No. Played power cards remain in the face-up used stack; only its top card is visible. A special action can recover a played card.
Use the King’s new position if moving him before ordinary deployment; use his old position if deploying first. The King card can place him in any region except Castillo.
Place Veto before you and retain it to stop one special action during this round or the next. It cannot stop ordinary deployment.

Yes, while Veto is held other players must announce special actions before executing them. Object as soon as the player starts; you can stop an announced action before execution or prevent the remaining part of an incomplete action. Completed actions cannot be vetoed, and executed parts are not undone.
Discard Veto after using it once. If unused, discard it at the end of the next round.
Every fellow player except the selecting player sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces. A player with an empty court sends none.
answers.evidence: Stack 2: Decay of Authority — all court.

answers.answer: The fellow player with two sends both to the provinces; you, as selecting player, are unaffected even though you have five in court.
answers.evidence: Stack 2: Decay of Authority — three from court.

answers.answer: The detailed paragraph and printed card require each player, including the selecting player, to send three of their own to the provinces. Proceed from the selecting player’s left clockwise, with the selecting player last. Each chooses pieces from any regions and/or court, never the King’s region or Castillo. No explicit shortfall rule is supplied. The heading instead says “fellow players.”

The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for every player, including themselves, and returns each piece to its owner’s provinces. Pieces cannot come from courts, the King’s region, or Castillo. No fallback is given if someone has no eligible piece.
answers.evidence: Stack 2: Send one from each player.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly selects one region on their disk; choices are simultaneous and revealed together. Choose a region containing at least two of that player’s Caballeros, and return two to the provinces. The King’s region and Castillo are excluded as sources.
answers.evidence: Stack 2: Fellow players secretly remove two.

answers.answer: If no region has two, choose a region with one and return that one to the provinces. Never take from the King’s region or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 2: Fellow players secretly remove two.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses a region on their disk with at least one of their own Caballeros; reveal choices together and return all their own there to the provinces. A player with no Caballeros in any region is unaffected. The King’s region and Castillo are excluded.
answers.evidence: Stack 2: Fellow players secretly remove all from one region.

answers.answer: Yes. The player may choose any region, including the King’s region or Castillo. Apply normal region-scoring rules, rank limits, and bonuses. Scoring Castillo leaves the same pieces covered there; they are not redistributed.
answers.evidence: Stack 2: Pick one region to score.

answers.answer: The printed all-4 group is Galicia, Catalonia, and Seville; eligibility is determined by the current first scoreboard value. With 8/4/0 at Galicia, Galicia no longer qualifies; Granada with 4/0/0 qualifies. Applicable King’s and home bonuses apply to special scoring.

The printed 5-value group is Basque Country, Aragon, and Valencia; the 6-and-7 group is Old Castile, New Castile, and Granada. Eligibility uses current first value (mobile scoreboard replaces printed values), so mobile boards can change membership. Castillo is explicitly excluded from all-5 scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3: special scoring intro and all-5/all-6-and-7 rows.

answers.answer: Only a sole first-place player scores; tied leaders score nothing, and lower ranks get nothing. Castillo is excluded.
answers.evidence: Stack 3: First position only in all regions.

answers.answer: Score all board regions tied for the most Caballeros. Castillo is neither considered nor scored, even if it contains more than either tied region.
Compare nonempty board regions and score all regions tied for the least. Empty regions and Castillo are not considered or scored.

All fellow players move all their own Caballeros out of the chosen region. Each affected player secretly chooses another region with their disk; choices are revealed together and their group moves there. Choosing the King’s region or the region being vacated sends that player’s pieces to their court. The King’s-region taboo bars taking pieces from that region, and Castillo cannot be emptied with this card.
Royal Adviser moves the King one neighboring region at most; the King card can put him in any region except Castillo.

The Court moves two of your own Caballeros from provinces to court. This is separate from the 4-stack card’s normal deployment of up to four from court to board; complete the two activities in either order.

All players secretly select regions on disks and reveal simultaneously. Score a region only if uniquely selected; duplicate selections do not score. Disk options are the nine board regions, including the King’s region, but not Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 4: Each secretly chooses a region to score.

answers.answer: Move all your own Caballeros from one region, distributing among other regions and/or Castillo; you may return some to the original region. Origins exclude the King’s region and Castillo; destinations exclude the King’s region but may include Castillo.

The card’s normal deployment is up to one from court to adjacent regions and/or Castillo. The special action adds up to two more from court to any non-King region and/or Castillo, for up to three total entering the board; only the normal one requires adjacency.
No, choose only one special alternative: two more from court or all your own from one region. Normal up-to-one deployment still applies.
answers.evidence: Stack 1: Two more from court or all your own row.

answers.answer: Move up to five own and/or foreign Caballeros from one origin region only; they may have different owners but cannot come from multiple origins. Send them to other non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 1: Up to five from one region.

answers.answer: Move up to three Caballeros belonging to other players only; fewer and multiple origins are allowed. Your own pieces cannot be included. Destinations may be any non-King region or Castillo; origins exclude the King’s region and Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 1: Intrigue intro; Any three foreign row.

answers.answer: Any three allows up to three own and/or foreign from any non-King origin regions to any non-King regions and/or Castillo. Any four allows up to four own and/or foreign from non-King origins to other non-King regions and/or Castillo; preserve the “other regions” destination restriction.
answers.evidence: Stack 1: Any three and Any four rows.

answers.answer: Move up to two of your own plus up to two foreign Caballeros, as separate ownership allowances, from any regions (multiple origins permitted). The King’s region and Castillo cannot be origins; destinations may be any non-King region and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 1: Intrigue intro; Two own and two foreign row.

answers.answer: Move up to four own Caballeros only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo. King’s region and Castillo cannot be sources.
answers.evidence: Stack 1: Intrigue intro; Any four of your own row.

answers.answer: The 4-stack secret-scoring action uses disks that allow the nine board regions, including the King’s region, but not Castillo; simultaneous duplicate selections do not score. The separate pick-one-region card allows its player to choose any region, including the King’s region or Castillo, applying normal scoring rules.
answers.evidence: Stack 4: Each secretly chooses a region to score; Stack 2: Pick one region to score.
